description: We are rockers. Our Team has one ML engineer, another ML engineer and finally a person who understands and gives ideas about where to apply this ML engineering in the hackathon of NASA SPACE APPS CHALLENGE
summary:
OrbiFallow is a web app that helps farmers in Uzbekistan’s Fergana Valley choose a better crop rotation. The farmer marks a field on a map and answers a few questions about past crops, water, salt and priorities. The app compares thousands of four-year rotations and shows four clear options, starting from what the farmer already grows.

It addresses the challenge by turning NASA data into advice a farmer can act on. We use 25 years of NASA POWER weather and GPM IMERG rainfall to replay each crop through real past seasons, and GRACE-FO and NASADEM to flag water loss and erosion risk. Every suggestion comes with the reason it was picked, its benefits over the current rotation, the risks seen in past weather, and what to check locally.

This matters because water is scarce in the valley and soils are under pressure from salt and repeated cotton and wheat. A rotation that saves water and rests the soil helps a farm stay productive, but only if the farmer can trust it. OrbiFallow shows its evidence and its limits, so the farmer makes the final call.
details:
OrbiFallow helps a farmer in the Fergana Valley decide what to plant over the next four years. The farmer marks the field on a map, tells us what grew there, how much water and salt the field has, what matters most to them, and which crops they must keep or cannot grow. The app then compares thousands of possible rotations and shows four: the current one, a small one-year change, the best overall fit, and the best for the farmer’s top goal.

For each rotation we show why it was picked, where it beats the current one, and what to check on the ground. We also replay every crop through 25 years of real weather, so the farmer sees “worked in 21 of 25 years” instead of a promise.

The goal is less water use and healthier soil without asking farmers to gamble. Water is the hard limit in this region, so we built around it.

The engine is written in Python with FastAPI and pandas, and the web app in React and TypeScript. We use NASA POWER, GPM IMERG, GRACE-FO and NASADEM, plus SoilGrids, FAO-56 and ECOCROP. We used AI coding tools, described in the SI section.

What makes it different is that it tests advice against the past, always starts from what the farmer already does, and says plainly what it doesn’t know. We considered contract crops such as wheat and cotton, phone use in the field, and plain language. Income, a view of the field from space, and review by a local agronomist are our next steps.
